newsitem.title: USA: FOB Gulf Grain - SRW wheat lower, corn, soy steady.
newsitem.headline: FOB Gulf Grain - SRW wheat lower, corn, soy steady.

text.p: Nearby FOB soft red winter wheat values were weaker on Thursday while corn and soybean prices were steady, export sources said.
"We've got the (December/March) spreads knocking the premiums down," one broker said, referring to the drop in nearby SRW wheat values.
The December/March spread at the Chicago Board of Trade widened to nearly 20 cents per bushel on Thursday.
News that Morocco bought wheat from Argentina further depressed U.S. export markets and reaffirmed the belief that U.S. wheat was overvalued relative to world prices.
"Part of it is the quality and the fact that they have a higher freight rate," one broker said about Argentine wheat.
"That compensates for some of the (price difference) but not all of it," he added.
Argentine FOB hard wheat values were at $136.00 for December, compared with $185.55 for U.S. hard red winter wheat, brokers noted.
